Connecting and creating database
```{r}
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)

con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), ":memory:")

dbExecute(con, "PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON") #enforcing foreign key relationships

#Creating a fact table 'fact_sales'
```

Creating and loading sales table
```{r}
dbExecute(con, "
          CREATE TABLE fact_sales (
          sale_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
          sale_date TEXT NOT NULL,
          customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
          region_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
          product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
          quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (quantity > 0),
          amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (amount_cents >= 0)
          )
          ")
```

Generating Sample Data
```{r}
set.seed(132)

n <- 30000L

#creates a sequence of every date from January 1, 2024 through December 31, 2025
calendar <- seq.Date(
  as.Date("2024-01-01"),
  as.Date("2025-12-31"),
  by = "day"
)

#generating random quantities between 1 to 5 
quantity <- sample.int(5L, n, replace = TRUE)

#Generating random prices between 500 and 10,000 cents
unit_price_cents <- sample(
  500L:10000L, n, replace = TRUE
)

#adds all columns into one table 
sales <- data.frame(
  sale_id = seq_len(n),
  sale_date = format(
    sample(calendar, n, replace = TRUE),
    "%Y-%m-%d"
  ),
  customer_id = sample.int(2000L, n, replace = TRUE),
  region_id = sample.int(6L, n, replace = TRUE),
  product_id = sample.int(500L, n, replace = TRUE),
  quantity = quantity,
  amount_cents = as.integer(quantity * unit_price_cents)
)

#sorting the sale from earliest to latest and smallest to largest when multiple sales have the same date 
sales <- sales[order(sales$sale_date, sales$sale_id), ]
```

Inserting Data into SQLite
```{r}
dbWithTransaction(con, {
  dbAppendTable(con, "fact_sales", sales)
})

#Checking results
dbGetQuery(con, "
           SELECT 
           COUNT(*) AS total_sales,
           MIN(sale_date) AS earliest_date,
           MAX(sale_date) AS latest_date,
           SUM(amount_cents) AS total_revenue
           FROM fact_sales
           ")
```

Querying Monthly Revenue- We want to calculate total revenue for each region during June 2025
```{r}
q_month <- "
SELECT
region_id,
SUM(amount_cents) as revenue_cents
FROM fact_sales
WHERE sale_date >= '2025-05-01'
AND sale_date < '2025-07-01'
GROUP BY region_id
ORDER BY region_id 
"

dbGetQuery(con, q_month)

```

Querying a particular customer- finding the 20 most recent sales made by customer 77
```{r}
q_customer <- "
SELECT
sale_date,
sale_id,
amount_cents
FROM fact_sales
WHERE customer_id = 77
ORDER BY sale_date DESC, sale_id DESC
LIMIT 20 
"

dbGetQuery(con, q_customer)
```

Measuring Query Execution Time
```{r}
time_query <- function(sql, repetitions = 5L) {

  elapsed <- vapply(seq_len(repetitions), function(i) {

    system.time(
      dbGetQuery(con, sql)
    )[["elapsed"]]

  }, numeric(1))

  data.frame(
    run = seq_len(repetitions),
    elapsed_seconds = elapsed
  )
}

#running the query and recording how long each execution takes
month_times <- time_query(q_month)

customer_times <- time_query(q_customer)

month_times
customer_times

median(month_times$elapsed_seconds)

median(customer_times$elapsed_seconds)
```

Paritioning a table by month 
Why do this? If we only need June 2025, we can access the June 2025 partition instead of searching through every month's data

Generating Monthly Boundaries
```{r}
month_starts <- seq.Date(
  as.Date("2024-01-01"),
  as.Date("2026-01-01"),
  by = "month"
)

partition_map <- data.frame(

  table_name = paste0(
    "sales_",
    format(month_starts[-length(month_starts)], "%Y_%m")
  ),

  lower = format(
    month_starts[-length(month_starts)],
    "%Y-%m-%d"
  ),

  upper = format(
    month_starts[-1L],
    "%Y-%m-%d"
  )

)

head(partition_map)

#Creating and populating the partitions
for (i in seq_len(nrow(partition_map))) {

  table_name <- partition_map$table_name[i]

  lower <- partition_map$lower[i]

  upper <- partition_map$upper[i]

  quoted_table <- dbQuoteIdentifier(con, table_name)

  quoted_lower <- dbQuoteString(con, lower)

  quoted_upper <- dbQuoteString(con, upper)

  create_sql <- sprintf("
    CREATE TABLE %s (
      sale_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
      sale_date TEXT NOT NULL
        CHECK (sale_date >= %s AND sale_date < %s),
      customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
      region_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
      product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
      quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (quantity > 0),
      amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (amount_cents >= 0)
    )
  ", quoted_table, quoted_lower, quoted_upper)

  dbExecute(con, create_sql)

  insert_sql <- sprintf("
    INSERT INTO %s
    SELECT *
    FROM fact_sales
    WHERE sale_date >= ?
      AND sale_date < ?
  ", quoted_table)

  dbExecute(
    con,
    insert_sql,
    params = list(lower, upper)
  )

}
```

We use a for loop to automatically create all 24 monthly tables- putting the CREATE TABLE query inside the for loop and inserting data from con
This is called parameterized SQL and it helps prevent SQL injection and handles values safely. 

Checking the Partitions: 
```{r}
dbGetQuery(con, "
           SELECT COUNT(*) AS june_sales
           FROM sales_2025_06
           ")
```

Checking whether all the monthly partition tables contain the same total number of sales as the original 'fact_sales' table
```{r}
partition_counts <- vapply(
  partition_map$table_name,
  function(tbl){
    sql <- sprintf(
      "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM %s",
      dbQuoteIdentifier(con, tbl)
    )
    dbGetQuery(con, sql)$n[[1]]
  },
  numeric(1)
)

sum(partition_counts)

dbGetQuery(con, "
           SELECT COUNT(*) AS original_sales
           FROM fact_sales
           ")


```

Routing Queries to the correct partitions
Partitioning creates separate tables, but we use a routine function that determines wich monthly partitions overlap with the requested date range
```{r}
routed_month_query <- function(start_date, end_date) {
  start_date <- as.Date(start_date)
  end_date <- as.Date(end_date)
  if(
    length(start_date) != 1L ||
    length(end_date) !=  1L ||
    is.na(start_date) ||
    is.na(end_date)
  ) {
    stop("Invalid date")
  }
  if(start_date >= end_date) {
    stop("Start date must be before end date")
  }
  start_text <- format(start_date, "%Y-%m-%d")
  end_text <- format(end_date, "%Y-%m-%d")
  if(
    start_text < min(partition_map$lower) ||
    end_text > max(partition_map$upper)
  ) {
    stop("Requested interval is outside partition coverage")
  }
  
  selected <- partition_map[
    partition_map$lower < end_text & #identifies partitions that overlap with the requested date range 
      partition_map$upper > start_text,
  ]
  
  pieces <- vapply(
    selected$table_name,
    function(tbl){
      sprintf("
              SELECT region_id, amount_cents
              FROM %s
              WHERE sale_date >= %s
              AND sale_date < %s
              ",
              dbQuoteIdentifier(con, tbl),
              dbQuoteString(con, start_text),
              dbQuoteString(con, end_text)
              )
    },
    character(1)
  )
  combined <- paste(
    pieces,
    collapse = "\nUNION ALL\n"
  )
  
  final_query <- paste0("
                        SELECT
                        region_id,
                        SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue_cents 
                        FROM (
                        ", combined, "
                        ) AS combined_sales
                        GROUP BY region_id
                        ORDER BY region_id 
                        ")
}
```


Indexes and Query Plans 
```{r}
dbExecute(con, "
          CREATE INDEX idx_customer
          ON sales(customer_id)
          ")

#Inspecting the Query Plan
dbGetQuery(con, "
           EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN 
           SELECT * 
           FROM sales
           WHERE customer_id = 10
           ")

#Creating a composite index (indexes more than one column)
dbExecute(con, "
          CREATE INDEX idx_customer_date
          ON sales(customer_id, sale_date)
          ")

dbExecute(con, "
          ANALYZE ") #helping SQLite's query planner decide whether using the composite index is worthwhile 

```

Views and Stored Summaries
```{r}
#Creating a view 
dbExecute(con, "
          CREATE VIEW customer_summary AS 
          SELECT 
          customer_id, 
          SUM(amount) AS revenue,
          COUNT(*) AS sales_count
          FROM sales
          GROUP BY customer_id
          ")

#Accessing view
dbGetQuery(con, "
           SELECT * 
           FROM customer_summary
           ")

#Creating a stored Summary table - stores calculated results
dbExecute(con, "
          CREATE TABLE stored_summary (
          customer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
          revenue INTEGER,
          sales_count INTEGER
          )
          ")

#populating table 
dbExecute(con, "
          INSERT INTO stored_summary
          SELECT
          customer_id,
          SUM(amount),
          COUNT(*)
          FROM sales
          GROUP BY customer_id
          ")

```

Suppose new sales are inserted into the original table. The stored summary will not automatically update; we must refresh it 
```{r}
dbWithTransaction(con, { #creating / executing a transaction
  dbExecute(con, "
            DELETE FROM stored_summary
            ")
  dbExecute(con, " --recalculating using the original table + inserting updated results 
            INSERT INTO stored_summary
            SELECT 
            customer_id,
            SUM(amount),
            ACOUNT(*)
            FROM sales
            GROUP BY customer_id
            ")
})

dbDisconnect(con)
```
